Empirical Research Plan: Hedge-Fund Activism, Governance, and Performance (2001-2006)

--------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
--------------------------------------------------
Chosen strategy: Difference-in-Differences (DiD) with an event-time dynamic specification (a “DiD-event study”).

Why appropriate?
• The treatment (public announcement of activism) is a clearly dated, firm-specific shock.  
• A panel of treated and comparable non-treated firms is available before and after each event.  
• Parallel-trend plausibility can be assessed with pre-event leads, and dynamic effects can be traced with post-event lags.  
• Short-window market reactions (CARs) can be estimated in a separate classical event study, but the core causal claims on governance and accounting variables require panel DiD.

--------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
--------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
Treated_it = 1 if firm i is the target of a hedge-fund activism campaign announced in calendar year τ and t ≥ τ; 0 otherwise.

Treatment timing / event date  
EventDate_iτ = announcement date from filings / news.  
For annual data create EventYear_i = year(EventDate_iτ). Event-time index k = t – EventYear_i.

Control group (counterfactual)  
Firms that:  
(a) are never targeted during 2001-2006 (“clean” controls) OR receive activism only after the observation window ends; and  
(b) are matched to treated firms on industry (4-digit SIC), size, market-to-book, and pre-event performance using propensity scores or exact coarsened matching.  
Main spec uses the full matched control sample; robustness will include (i) all non-targets with firm FE, (ii) re-matched ±1-for-1 nearest-neighbor sample.

No RDD: no running variable. No IV: no strong, plausibly exogenous instrument available in the provided information.

--------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
--------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel Trends – Absent activism, treated and control firms would have followed the same evolution in governance/performance.  
Plausibility: Matching on observables and inclusion of firm & year FEs help; pre-trend tests will be conducted.

A2. No Anticipation – Managers/markets do not adjust outcomes materially before the public announcement.  
Plausibility: Activists often accumulate quietly; however, large governance or operational changes usually follow or coincide with announcement. Leads in the event-study absorb potential anticipatory effects and serve as a test.

A3. Stable Unit Treatment Value (SUTVA) / No Spillovers – Activism on firm i does not directly change outcomes of matched controls.  
Plausibility: Industry peers might react, but direct governance changes are firm-specific; we will mitigate by dropping firms in the same 3-digit SIC and quarter if they experience activism.

A4. Exogenous Timing Conditional on Covariates – Conditional on observables and FE, the exact year of activism is as-good-as random.  
Plausibility: Activists target under-performers, so selection is not random; but DiD leverages within-firm changes, and we explicitly soak up differential trends with matching and firm FEs.

--------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation
--------------------------------------------------
T1. Selection on Unobserved Trends (violates A1).  
Fix: (i) Include ≥2 pre-event leads to test for pre-trends; (ii) add firm-specific linear trends; (iii) implement stacked-DiD (Sun & Abraham 2021) to handle staggered timing.

T2. Multiple Treatments / Repeat Campaigns.  
Fix: Keep only the first activism event per firm; robustness keeps all events but uses stacked-DiD with cohort indicators.

T3. Spillovers to Controls (violates SUTVA).  
Fix: Exclude controls in same 4-digit SIC & quarter as any treated firm; run placebo dropping industry peers of treated firms as robustness.

--------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
--------------------------------------------------
```r
# packages
library(data.table)   # fast data
library(fixest)       # DiD regressions
library(MatchIt)      # propensity-score matching
library(bacondecomp)  # DiD decomposition / SA2021 check

# 1. Load data --------------------------------------------------------------
df <- fread("hedge_fund_activism_2001_2006.csv")   # one row per firm-year

# 2. Construct variables ----------------------------------------------------
# Event year and treatment indicators
df[, EventYear := min(Year[Activism==1]), by = FirmID]      # first event
df[, Treated  := !is.na(EventYear)]
df[, rel_year := Year - EventYear]                          # k = -5,...,+5
# keep a symmetric window
df <- df[rel_year >= -5 & rel_year <= 5]

# Build matched control sample ---------------------------------------------
# Estimate propensity to be targeted pre-event (-1 year)
pre <- df[rel_year == -1]
ps_model <- glm(Treated ~ log(Size) + MTB + ROA + Industry, 
                data = pre, family = binomial)
pre$pscore <- predict(ps_model, type = "response")

# Nearest-neighbor matching (1:3)
match.out <- matchit(Treated ~ log(Size) + MTB + ROA + Industry,
                     data = pre, method = "nearest", ratio = 3)
matched_ids <- match.data(match.out)$FirmID
df_matched <- df[FirmID %in% matched_ids]

# 3. Dynamic DiD regression -------------------------------------------------
event_dummies <- paste0("i(rel_year, ref = -1, droplevels = c(-1))")  # -1 baseline

spec <- feols(ROA ~ event_dummies + log(Size) + MTB | FirmID + Year,
              cluster = ~FirmID,
              data = df_matched)

etable(spec, se = "cluster")

# 4. Pre-trend test ---------------------------------------------------------
wald_pre <- wald(spec, keep = "rel_year::(-5|-4|-3|-2)")
print(wald_pre)

# 5. Robustness: Stacked DiD (Sun & Abraham) -------------------------------
# bacon decomposition to see weight problem
bacon_out <- bacon(ROA ~ Treated, data = df_matched, id_var = "FirmID", time_var = "Year")
plot(bacon_out)

# Alternative outcome: CAR over (-2,+2) days -------------------------------
car <- fread("daily_returns.csv")
# build CAR; join to df; run same spec but on car

```

--------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
--------------------------------------------------
Based on prior literature, I expect:
• Short-run (announcement-window) CAR: +5% to +8%.  
• Accounting performance (ROA) improves by 1–1.5 p.p. within 2–3 years.  
• Board independence rises (~10 percentage-points) and CEO turnover probability increases (≈5 p.p.) post-activism.  
Sign of main coefficient β_post > 0 for performance and governance quality.

--------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DiD)
C1: Parallel pre-trends clearly satisfied?                    0.8   (some concern)
C2: No anticipation / correct timing?                         0.7
C3: No spillovers / SUTVA?                                    0.6
C4: Treatment exogeneity conditional on FE & covariates?      0.6
C5: Robustness & falsification exercises implemented?         1.0

(Scores: C1=1, C2=1, C3=0, C4=0, C5=1 → Total 3/5)

Overall, while plausible, credibility hinges on pre-trend evidence and spillover checks—both included in the empirical design.
